chief_complaint: burning pain and hand numbness, Phalen test positive
hpi_details: A 23-year-old male presents to the clinic with burning pain and hand numbness, phalen test positive. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: He thinks he strained the tendons in his wrist or compressed a blood vessel from spending long hours typing and gaming.
concerns: He is worried that the numbness will worsen to the point where he loses dexterity and cannot keep up with his computer programming work.
expectations: He hopes to be fitted with a supportive wrist splint and given practical ergonomics advice so he does not have to take time off work.

clinical_knowledge.topic: Carpal Tunnel Syndrome evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Carpal Tunnel Syndrome is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Plan for Carpal Tunnel right wrist: Nocturnal neutral wrist splint, schedule EMG/NCS, ergonomics, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Carpal Tunnel Syndrome.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Cervical radiculopathy (C6/C7) without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Thenar muscle atrophy.

boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.

reference_soap.assessment: Condition highly suspicious for Carpal Tunnel right wrist.
reference_soap.plan: For suspected right carpal tunnel syndrome, trial a nocturnal neutral wrist splint and ergonomic modification. Consider EMG/NCS for persistent, atypical, or motor symptoms; arrange prompt specialist assessment for thenar weakness or atrophy. Counsel the patient.

teaching.one_liner: Entrapment of the median nerve within the carpal tunnel causing nocturnal numbness and tingling in the radial three and a half digits.

must_ask.say: Are the numbness and burning located in your thumb, index, and middle fingers?
Does the hand numbness wake you up at night needing to shake your hands for relief?
Do you drop objects frequently or struggle to open jars or button shirts?
Do you perform repetitive wrist flexing activities or heavy computer typing?
Does holding your wrists bent together worsen the tingling within a minute?

history.answer: My right hand has been burning and going numb lately, and it's been getting harder to ignore.
It is mostly a burning, pins-and-needles numbness in my hand, but I haven't noticed any actual paralysis or true loss of muscle strength.
It is only in my right hand, mostly in my thumb, index, middle finger, and half of my ring finger.
It started about three weeks ago and has been gradually getting worse, and I've also been feeling worn out and fatigued overall.
At first the tingling came and went, but over the past week it has become much more constant and bothersome throughout the day.
I have not dropped cups or plates, but my hand feels a bit clumsy when buttoning my shirt or typing for hours.
Yes, I frequently wake up in the middle of the night because my hand is burning and asleep, and I have to shake it out to get relief.
Bending my wrist while typing or holding my phone brings on the tingling right away, but shaking my hand helps ease it.
No, my neck feels fine, and there is no pain shooting down from my neck or shoulder into my arm.
No, I have not had any slurred speech, facial drooping, double vision, or dizziness at all.
No, my bowel and bladder habits are completely normal, and I have no numbness around my groin.
No shortness of breath, no trouble swallowing or chewing, and no drooping eyelids.
I have not seen any muscle twitching, and the muscle pad below my thumb looks normal and hasn't shrunk.
No, I have not had any diarrhea, fever, cold, or stomach flu over the past few weeks.
I don't have high blood pressure, diabetes, high cholesterol, or any heart rhythm problems.
I eat a regular diet with meat and vegetables, have never had stomach surgery, and drink alcohol only once or twice a month.
I do not take water pills, steroids, chemotherapy, or any other medications that could affect my nerves or muscles.
I work long hours on a computer typing code and clicking a mouse all day, and I also play video games on my computer on weekends.
I have always been healthy and have never been diagnosed with any medical conditions before.
I have never had any surgeries and have never stayed in a hospital overnight.
I am not taking any prescription medicines, over-the-counter painkillers, or dietary supplements.
I don't have any allergies to medications, foods, or latex.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used e-cigarettes.
I only have a glass of beer once or twice a month when hanging out with friends.
I work as a software programmer and live on my own in a small apartment.
Both of my parents are healthy in their fifties, and there is no family history of nerve disorders or early strokes.
I thought maybe I strained the tendons in my wrist or squeezed a blood vessel from typing all day at work and playing computer games at night.
I'm really worried that my hands will get too numb to type properly and I won't be able to keep up with my coding workload at my job.
I'm hoping to leave with a good wrist brace and some ergonomic tips so I can keep working without missing any days.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 118/76 mmHg, pulse 72 beats per minute, respiratory rate 14 breaths per minute, body temperature 36.6°C, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Cranial nerves II through XII are grossly intact with symmetric facial expression, intact visual fields, and normal extraocular movements.
Full active cervical range of motion without midline spinous process tenderness; Spurling test is negative bilaterally without radicular pain.

Phalen test on the right wrist reproduces numbness and tingling in the thumb, index, and middle fingers within 30 seconds; positive Tinel sign over the right volar carpal tunnel; no joint swelling or redness.
Motor strength is 5/5 in all major muscle groups of the bilateral upper and lower extremities, with preserved right abductor pollicis brevis strength and no thenar atrophy.

Decreased sensation to light touch and pinprick over the palmar aspect of the right thumb, index, middle finger, and radial half of the ring finger; sensation over the thenar eminence and hypothenar area is preserved.
Biceps, triceps, brachioradialis, patellar, and Achilles reflexes are 2+ bilaterally; Babinski sign is absent bilaterally.
Casual gait, heel-to-toe tandem gait, and Romberg test are normal without ataxia or drift.
